issues.detail: The Greek 'διακονη μοι' (diakone moi) means 'serve me', but the Vietnamese 'phục vụ tôi' is placed after 'thay anh' (instead of you/for you). The Greek structure 'ινα υπερ σου διακονη μοι' means 'that you might serve me for [the sake of] you' or 'that you would serve me on your behalf'. The Vietnamese 'thay anh' implies the speaker is doing the service *instead* of the listener, whereas the Greek indicates the *listener* is the one performing the service.
